2609.06941.title: When and Why LLM Causal Priors Help: Closed-Loop Prior Selection for Amortized Causal Inference
2609.06941.paper_summary: Causal effect estimation asks how an outcome would change under an intervention, and medicine, economics, and public policy all treat it as a foundational task. Prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) amortize the task: a model trained on large numbers of programmatically generated synthetic causal tasks reads a new problem's observational data into context and returns an interventional-effect estimate in a single forward pass. The capability of such models is largely determined by the synthetic training prior, which is currently designed by hand, a bottleneck acknowledged by both Do-PFN and CausalPFN. Large language models (LLMs) can now ``draw'' plausible causal graphs for a given domain, suggesting that LLM-distilled graphs could serve as prior material. Whether injecting such graphs helps at all, where any gain comes from, and when injection helps. Practice has so far relied on manual trial and error. We propose a \emph{closed-loop prior selection framework} that casts prior injection as a budget-constrained optimization over a candidate prior pool. Candidates undergo cheap post-training and are scored by a composite metric dominated by real-domain generalization; the winner then receives full training and paired statistical validation. On a 7.34M-parameter Do-PFN, the framework's winner attains a formally significant $2.75\times$ gain on the primary evaluation domain, and its error falls below that of the uninjected official base. Generalization on an adjacent monitoring domain improves significantly, and no monitored capability degrades. Mechanism experiments show that the gain depends on the semantic content of the distilled graph rather than its structural diversity alone does not produce it (directional evidence). With this framework and this regularity in hand, the use of LLM causal priors stops being manual trial and error and becomes an empirically verifiable selection problem.
2609.06941.paper_summary_zh: 因果效應估計探討在干預下結果將如何改變，醫學、經濟學和公共政策都將其視為一項基礎任務。先前數據擬合網絡（PFNs）使這項任務得以攤銷：一個在大量程序生成的合成因果任務上訓練的模型，將新問題的觀察數據納入上下文，並在一次前向傳遞中返回干預效應估計。此類模型的能力在很大程度上取決於合成訓練先驗，該先驗目前是手動設計的，這一瓶頸已被Do-PFN和CausalPFN所認可。大型語言模型（LLMs）現在可以為給定領域“繪製”合理的因果圖，這表明LLM提煉的圖可能作為先驗材料。注入這些圖是否有幫助、任何增益來自何處以及何時注入有幫助，實踐至今仍依賴於手動的試錯。我們提出了一個\emph{閉環先驗選擇框架}，將先驗注入視為對候選先驗池的預算約束優化。候選者經過便宜的後訓練，並通過以真實領域泛化為主的綜合指標進行評分；獲勝者隨後接受全面訓練和配對統計驗證。在一個734萬參數的Do-PFN上，該框架的獲勝者在主要評估領域達到了正式顯著的$2.75\times$增益，其誤差低於未注入的官方基準。在相鄰的監控領域上，泛化顯著改善，且沒有任何監控能力下降。機制實驗顯示，增益依賴於提煉圖的語義內容，而非僅僅其結構多樣性（方向證據）。有了這個框架和這種規律，使用LLM因果先驗不再是手動的試錯，而成為一個可實證驗證的選擇問題。
2609.06941.author: Haohao Zhou et.al.
